newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds staying positive into weekend.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds staying positive into weekend.

text.p: *Australian bonds look set to end the week on a more positive note than it started it with hopes of an easing in local interest rates and stable U.S. policy buoying the tone.
*Afternoon session may be quiet with much of Europe closed.
The Australian bond market looks set to end the week on a more positive note than it started it with hopes of an easing in local interest rates and stable U.S. policy buoying the tone.

This week's batch of U.S. data confirmed that inflation there is well under control and has pushed fears of a Fed tightening out towards the end of the year. The Federal Open Market Committee meets on August 19.
The local bonds continue to build on this week's rebound from one month lows with U.S. Treasuries looking more solid and easing hopes underpinning the short end, traders said.

December bill futures are already discounting a 25 basis point cut in current 5.0 percent official rates in the wake of Thursday's benign final second quarter wages data, striking a new contract high of 95.27.
"There were even some people looking for an easing this morning," one trader said.
The December 10-year bond futures contract tested resistance at 93.470 at one stage, extending the rebound from the 93.135 low seen on Wednesday.
However, traders said the afternoon session could turn quiet with many European centres closed for holiday on Friday.

The local market continued its outperforming bias against the dollar bloc, extending Thursday's sharp spread compression which followed the wages data. The largest move was against against Canada, which also lagged the U.S. rally, while margins New Zealand were mixed.
